candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Book of Parables (1 Enoch 37-71)
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Parables (1 Enoch 37-71) (c. 100 BC)

'And the Lord of Spirits placed the Elect One on the throne of glory. And he shall judge all the works of the holy above in the heaven, and in the balance shall their deeds be weighed' — the cosmic-weighing image with the Elect One as judge. Tewahedo iconography of the last judgment (developed especially in the Mäṣḥafä Berhan / Book of Light) depicts Christ as throne-judge with scales held by Michael — drawing on 61:8 as scriptural anchor for the iconographic program.
candidates.reviewer_notes: Curated PD interpretive summary representing the Ethiopian Tewahedo tradition's reading via 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition), Book of Parables (1 Enoch 37-71). Verify the summary still reflects the source's argument before promoting; substitute a verbatim quote from the NPNF / Charles dump where available, and where applicable cross-check the Andəmta homiletic tradition for resonance.

candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Book of Parables (1 Enoch 37-71)
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Parables (1 Enoch 37-71) (c. 100 BC)

'And he will summon all the host of the heavens, and all the holy ones above, and the host of God, the Cherubic, Seraphin and Ophannin, and all the angels of power' — full angelic hierarchy with the rare Ophannin (= ophanim, the thrones / wheels of Ezk 1:15-21). Tewahedo angelology preserves the threefold-angel structure (Cherubim / Seraphim / Ophanim) in the Sǝbḫata Foṣǝlt prayer, drawing on this verse as canonical authority for naming the third tier.
